1.
Heard Mr. Ashok Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the applicants as well as learned AGA for the state and perused the record.

2. The present application under Section 482 has been filed by the petitioner with the prayer to quash the impugned charge sheet No.87/2022, dated 30.10.2022 and summoning order dated 19.12.2022 passed by Civil Judge (J.D.) Ist/FTC, Pratapgarh in Case No.19644 of 2022 (State vs.
Ankit and Others), arising out of Case Crime No.114/2021, under Sections 498A, 323, 504 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, pending before the Court of Civil Judge (J.D.) Ist/F.T.C., Pratapgarh on the basis of compromise.

3. On 14.12.2023 following order was passed :-
" 1. Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. Present application has been moved by the applicants for quashing the charge sheet dated 30.10.2022 in Case Crime No.114 of 2021 U/S 498A, 504 I.P.C. and 3/4 of D.P. Act, P.S. Mahila Thana, District- Pratapgarh as well as summoning order dated 19.12.2022 passed by Civil Judge (J.D.)-I/ FTC, Pratapgarh in Case No.19644 of 2022.
3.

Learned counsel for the applicants submitted that the prosecution is a result of some matrimonial dispute between the parties and the issue has already been resolved by way of mediation before the family court, therefore, impugned proceedings may be quashed.

4. List this case on 17.01.2024.
5.
Issue notice to private respondent returnable at an early date.
6. On the next date, applicant no.1 as well as private respondent shall be present before this Court.

7. Station House Officer, P.S. Mandhata, District- Pratapgarh shall ensure the presence of private respondent, namely, Rinshu Yadav, d/o Ram Kailash Yadav, r/o Saray Harinarayan, P.S. Mandhata, District- Pratapgarh before this Court on the next date of listing."

4. In compliance of the aforesaid order, the applicant no.1; Ankit Yadav (husband) is present before this Court and has been identified by his counsel and the private respondent-Rinshu Yadav is also present before this Court, who has been brought and identified by lady constable Kumari Manisha Singh, Police Station-Mandhata, District-Pratapgarh.
5.

The applicant no.1 has come up with a demand draft of Rs.75,000/- bearing no.604391, dated 17.01.2024 issued by State Bank of India, Branch High Court (Lucknow) in favour of Rinshu Yadav,
D/o Ram Kailash.
6. The present matter is a result of matrimonial dispute between the parties.

In the proceedings under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act, marriage between both the parties has already been dissolved on 18.09.2023 and the condition as mentioned in the settlement agreement paragraph no.5 (annexure no.8) placed before the Counseling Cell : Family Courts Settlement that Rs.75,000/-
has to be paid to Rinshu Yadav.

sentences.text: As per the aforesaid condition, the applicant no.1; Ankit Yadav is present before this Court and placed the demand draft of Rs.75,000/-, which has been handed over to opposite party no.2; Rinshu Yadav before this Court, after retaining a photocopy of the same and opposite party no.2 acknowledges the same.
The opposite party no.2 submits that marriage between the two has been dissolved and the terms and conditions as mentioned in the agreement have been fulfilled.

8. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that on account of settlement agreement, all disputes between them have come to an end, and therefore, further proceedings against the applicants in the aforesaid case is liable to be quashed by this Court.

10. Learned A.G.A. does not dispute the aforesaid fact and submitted at the Bar that since the parties concerned have settled their dispute as mentioned above, therefore, he has no objection to quashing of the impugned criminal proceedings against the applicants.

11. Before proceeding any further it shall be apt to make a brief reference to the following cases:-
i. B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and Another; (2003)4 SCC 675, ii. Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation; (2008) 9 SCC 677, iii. Manoj Sharma Vs. State and Others; (2008) 16 SCC 1, iv. Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab; (2012); 10 SCC 303, v. Narindra Singh and others Vs. State of Punjab; ( 2014) 6 SCC 466,
12.

13. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, as noted herein above, and also the submissions made by the counsel for the parties, the Court is of the considered opinion that no useful purpose shall be served by prolonging the proceedings of the above mentioned criminal case as the parties have already settled their dispute.

14. Accordingly, the impugned charge sheet No.87/2022, dated 30.10.2022 and summoning order dated 19.12.2022 passed by Civil Judge (J.D.) Ist/FTC, Pratapgarh in Case No.19644 of 2022 (State vs. Ankit and Others), arising out of Case Crime No.114/2021, under Sections 498A, 323, 504 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, pending before the Court of Civil Judge (J.D.) Ist/F.T.C., Pratapgarh are hereby quashed.
